newsitem.title: UK: London gold paralysed, palladium at fresh lows.
newsitem.headline: London gold paralysed, palladium at fresh lows.

text.p: Gold and silver, hobbled by a lack of market interest, shuffled in narrow price ranges in early trading on Tuesday.
But palladium slid to new three-year lows amid bearish supply and demand factors and may head even lower, dealers said.
Gold bullion fixed barely changed at $381.00 an ounce, compared to $380.90 on Monday afternoon and a London close of $381.40/$381.90.
"Gold is rangetrading in the $380-$383 area. There's nothing too dramatic expected if things keep going the way they are," a London-based dealer said.
Activity was expected to pick up after New York's Comex futures market opened later in the day, however.
The precious metals had surged higher last week in an effort to break out of a recent downtrend, but the momentum appeared to have worn off, dealers said.
Silver, which made the most dramatic move last week by racing above the key $5.00 an ounce level, was now testing out the floor within its new price range.
"It's trying to find a base. Resistance is around $5.08, and it looks like it's going to be $4.97-$4.98," a dealer said. Below that, $4.93 should provide good support.
Prices were indicated at $5.01/$5.03, a decline of three cents from Monday's London close.
Palladium fixed at $116.25 an ounce on Tuesday morning, down $0.25 from the previous fix and the lowest fixing since September 14, 1993.
Prices of the white metal, used primarily in electronics, catalytic converters and dentistry, have been declining steadily since rallying to a high of around $175 an ounce in April 1995.
Dealers attributed its slide in recent months to steady sales from key producer Russia and slack demand from the Japanese electronics industry.
"It's a continuation of that trend, it's being hit from both the supply and demand angles," a dealer said. "There hasn't been anything dramatic, it's just drifting off."
Recent attempts to claw above the important $120 an ounce resistance level have met with selling, and the market has a distinctly bearish cast to it, he added.
Analysts and dealers said palladium showed the potential to drop further still, towards support at $112 and then possibly below $100 an ounce.
Palladium's sister metal platinum was indicated down $0.75 at $384.25/$385.25 an ounce.
